name: Maz Repository
observations: GitHub repo Mazoo85/maz
Holds two things: the Maz Engine (native C++ game engine) and ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE (browser game)
Root README.md documents both projects

name: Maz Engine
observations: Native C++20 + Vulkan + SDL3 game engine
2D-first but architected so 3D drops in later (renderer interface, camera abstraction, scene graph)
Built with CMake >= 3.24, warnings-as-errors; SDL3 and GLM fetched automatically via FetchContent
Current milestone is M0: the walking skeleton (window, fixed-timestep loop, Vulkan clear-screen renderer, clean shutdown)
Degrades gracefully with no GPU/display so it runs headless in CI
Lives under engine/ with core/, platform/, math/, render/ modules
Demo app is apps/sandbox; supports --headless and --frames N flags
Design docs: docs/ROADMAP.md (14-phase plan) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

name: ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE
observations: Browser-playable Project Zomboid-style open-world zombie survival game
Rendered as a 1990s SEGA 16-bit neon arcade title
Pure HTML5 Canvas + vanilla JavaScript, no build step or dependencies
Map is a 160x140 tile replica of downtown & midtown Anchorage, Alaska with real street and building names
Entry point is index.html; can also run via python3 -m http.server
Is the engine's eventual Phase 13 native-port target and design reference

name: ZOMBOID source layout
observations: index.html: shell + script load order
css/style.css: arcade-cabinet styling, scanlines
js/world.js: Anchorage data (avenues, streets, named buildings)
js/worldgen.js: bakes data into a tile grid + loot containers
js/items.js: item definitions + themed loot tables
js/audio.js: WebAudio chiptune SFX + music
js/game.js: engine (states, input, sim, combat, rendering, HUD)

name: Codebase Memory MCP
observations: MCP server that gives Claude persistent, cross-session memory about this codebase
Configured in .mcp.json as server name codebase-memory
Uses the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory package via npx
Launched through scripts/codebase-memory-server.sh, which pins the memory file to an absolute path in the repo
Knowledge graph is stored at .claude/codebase-memory.json and committed to git
Documented in docs/CODEBASE_MEMORY.md

name: Zomboid Native Port
observations: Native C++20 port of the ZOMBOID: ANCHORAGE browser game's deterministic simulation onto Maz Engine (roadmap Phase 13)
Lives in game/ as the dependency-free static library target 'zomboid' (alias maz::zomboid) — no SDL3/Vulkan/GLM, so it compiles and unit-tests headless in CI with no GPU/display

Public headers under game/include/zomboid/: Math.hpp (Vec2 + clamp/lerp/dist/normAngle), Rng.hpp (PCG32 deterministic RNG replacing JS Math.random()), Tiles.hpp (Tile enum + isSolidTile), World.hpp, Items.hpp, Sim.hpp
Sources under game/src/: World.cpp (Anchorage avenues/streets/buildings data + generateWorld), Items.cpp (item DB + themed weighted loot tables + rollLoot), Sim.cpp (the fixed-timestep simulation)

Sim is driven by a per-tick zb::Input intent struct (moveX/moveY, aim, attackHeld/attackPressed, interact, reload, useSlot, toggleFlashlight); step() runs updatePlayer/updateZombies/updateBullets/updateWorld at fixed kStep=1/60

Faithfully ports: five decaying needs (health/hunger/thirst/fatigue/mood), infection + bite chance, melee arc combat with weapon durability/breakage, ranged pistol/shotgun with ammo + bullets, zombie sight/wander/knockback AI + sprinters, day/night cycle with day-scaled night wave spawning, richness-scaled building loot containers
Purely-visual reference state (particles, float-texts, screen shake, CRT/scanline post-fx) is intentionally excluded from the sim and deferred to the future render layer
Documented in docs/ZOMBOID_PORT.md; design mapping table links each js/ file to its game/ counterpart

Has a dependency-free software reference rasterizer under game/include/zomboid/render/: Framebuffer.hpp (CPU RGB buffer with fill/blend/outline/circle/thick-line) and SoftRenderer.hpp/.cpp (renderScene() game viewport + renderWorldMap() overview) using the neon SEGA palette; deterministic and unit-tested (render check in zomboid_tests)

apps/zomboid gained a --render out.png mode (with --map/--width/--height/--tile) that writes a PNG via a tiny built-in stored-DEFLATE encoder in apps/zomboid/Png.hpp — lets the port be seen with no GPU; verified frames show the Anchorage street grid, purple-walled buildings with orange loot crates, trees, player + zombies

Code is clean under both g++ and clang with -Wconversion AND -Wsign-conversion -Werror (clang's -Wconversion implies sign-conversion); the software renderer defines the exact draw intent the future Vulkan sprite batch will reproduce and seeds Phase 12 golden-image tests

Has versioned binary save/load: Sim::saveState() serializes all mutable state (RNG stream via new Rng::state/inc/setState, clock/day/kills/waveTimer, player+inventory, zombies, bullets, corpses, opened-container flags, message log) to a byte blob tagged magic 'ZBSV' + version; loadState() regenerates the deterministic tile map and restores the rest, rejecting corrupt/truncated/wrong-magic/container-count-mismatch data WITHOUT mutating the sim
Serialization primitives live in game/include/zomboid/Save.hpp (Writer + bounds-checked Reader, floats copied bit-exact via memcpy, little-endian assumed); implementation in game/src/Save.cpp

Save/load is continuation-deterministic: a loaded game continues bit-identically to one never saved — proven by a unit test (run 400, snapshot, load into fresh sim, run both 300 more → identical saveState bytes) and via the CLI (600 continuous ticks == 400 ticks saved+reloaded+200 more; identical final state). Byte-exact file round-trip confirmed with cmp
apps/zomboid gained --save out.sav (after run) and --load in.sav (before run) flags; readFile/writeFile helpers in main.cpp
Test count is now 52 checks, 0 failures; clean under g++ and clang with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror

Software renderer now draws the full HUD via a built-in 5x7 bitmap font (game/include/zomboid/render/Font.hpp: drawChar/drawText, uppercase A-Z + digits + punctuation, lowercase folded to uppercase, 1px drop shadow): five neon stat bars with labels (HEALTH/FED/HYDRO/ENERGY/MOOD, plus INFECTION when infected), a top-right DAY/clock/KILLS/Z-ALIVE panel, the equipped-weapon readout, an 8-slot hotbar (equipped slot outlined, item tags + qty), and the bottom-left message log — mirroring the reference renderHUD

renderHud() lives in SoftRenderer.cpp and is gated by RenderOptions.hud (default true); verified visually via --render (hud.png) and by a unit test (hud-on frame != hud-off frame). Test count now 53 checks, 0 failures; still clean under g++ and clang with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror
Font glyphs are standard public-domain 5x7 bitmap shapes stored as 7 bytes each (low 5 bits = columns); the same atlas can feed a GPU bitmap/SDF font path later

Sim now maintains the reference's effect state: blood/muzzle particles (ParticleKind), floating damage-number/loot FloatText (FloatKind), and screen shake (kick()) — spawned from combat (damageZombie blood+damage number, killZombie extra blood, ranged muzzleFlash+kick 4/8, melee hit kick 2, hurtPlayer kick 3) and looting (per-drop '+qty name' float), advanced in updateWorld (particles drift+damp+fade, floats rise+fade, shake*=0.86). All deterministic via m_rng

Save format bumped to version 2: serializes particles, float texts, and shake so a loaded game continues bit-identically (v1 saves now rejected; none existed). Continuation-determinism test still passes

Software renderer draws blood particles under entities, muzzle particles over, and floating damage/loot numbers via the bitmap font (yellow=damage, green=loot). Verified in fx.png (a '14' damage number over a struck zombie + blood specks next to the player). 53 checks pass; clean under g++ and clang with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror. Only frame-level CRT/scanline post-fx remain outside the sim

Software renderer now finishes frames with a CRT post-pass (applyPostFx: 1px scanlines every 3rd row + soft corner vignette) gated by RenderOptions.postFx, and a deterministic screen-shake camera jitter derived from sim.shake() and dayTime (reproducible per frame)

Added neon SEGA menu screens: renderTitleScreen (synthwave gradient sky, banded neon sun, cyan perspective grid, chunky 'ZOMBOID/ANCHORAGE' title via neonTitle drop-shadow stack, blinking PRESS START), renderPauseScreen (dim + PAUSED), renderDeathScreen (red overlay + YOU DIED + survived-days/kills). renderScene auto-draws the death overlay when player.dead (RenderOptions.deathOverlay)

Font.hpp refactored to expose drawTextPlain (no shadow) used by neonTitle; app gained --screen title|pause|death. Verified via title.png (full synthwave title) and death.png (YOU DIED over the frozen scene with vignette). Test count now 57 checks, 0 failures; clean under g++ and clang with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror

Visual parity with the browser reference is now essentially complete headless: world+entities, particles/damage-numbers, HUD, night, CRT post-fx, and title/pause/death screens all render to PNG with no GPU. Remaining reference-only gap is the boot SEGA-jingle flash (cosmetic). The playable windowed build still needs the Vulkan/SDL/audio bridge (no Vulkan SDK in the dev container)

Audio is ported: game/include/zomboid/audio/Audio.hpp + game/src/Audio.cpp is a dependency-free headless chiptune synth mirroring js/audio.js — oscillator blips (square/triangle/saw/sine) with a 5ms exp attack + exp decay envelope and optional exp pitch slide, plus decaying white-noise bursts through a one-pole high-pass. Renders into a mono float Clip at 44100Hz and encodes 16-bit PCM WAV (encodeWav)

All 14 SFX (hit/swing/gun/shotgun/pickup/open/hurt/death/eat/drink/select/start/zgroan/sega) plus the looping bass(triangle)+lead(square) city music are ported with the reference's exact note recipes/gains (master 0.45, music 0.18); noise uses the seeded zb::Rng so WAV output is deterministic/reproducible

apps/zomboid-audio (CMake target zomboid_audio, output 'zomboid-audio') renders --sfx NAME/--music STEPS/--demo to WAV. Verified: valid RIFF/WAVE PCM 16-bit mono 44100 headers (via file(1)), correct durations (gun 0.18s, sega 1.15s, music 40 steps 7.24s, demo 7.5s), and byte-identical output per seed. Tests now 70 checks, 0 failures; clean under g++ and clang with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror

Remaining reference subsystem gap is only real-time playback: a Phase 7 audio device (SDL/miniaudio) to stream these recipes, and the Vulkan/SDL windowed bridge. The synthesis, sim, save/load, software renderer (HUD/post-fx/screens), terminal front-end, and audio-to-WAV are all done and verified headless

Fidelity audit done: Sim.cpp was compared line-by-line to js/game.js. All systems match (inventory, needs decay+consequences, melee/ranged combat, durability, zombie AI, bullets, collision, day/night, waves, loot). One real divergence was found and FIXED — the shotgun spread loop is s=-2..2 INCLUSIVE of 0, so a blast is the main slug + 5 pellets = 6 projectiles; an earlier `if (s==0) continue` had dropped it to 5. Pinned by tests/testWeapons (pistol=1, shotgun=6, no-ammo=0). Test count now 73 checks, 0 failures

Only intentionally-omitted reference details remain: frame-level CRT/scanline post-fx (in the render layer, not the sim) and the boot SEGA-jingle flash. Vestigial JS bullet.spread flag is unused in the reference sim so it's not modeled

name: zomboid headless driver
observations: apps/zomboid/main.cpp — headless autopilot executable (CMake target zomboid_game, output name 'zomboid')

Runs the ported Sim with a built-in autopilot that aims at the nearest zombie, backs away from close threats, swings, and periodically loots; prints a run summary (day/time, needs, kills, z-alive, weapon)
Flags: --ticks N, --seed S, --quiet, --help
Proof-of-life for the native port; a windowed renderer will bridge onto the same Sim later

name: zomboid unit tests
observations: tests/zomboid_tests.cpp — dependency-free unit tests for the Zomboid sim, wired as ctest 'zomboid_sim_tests' (links maz::zomboid)
Self-contained CHECK harness (no framework); exits non-zero on failure

Covers worldgen invariants + determinism, seeded reproducibility, starting kit, needs decay (thirst outpaces hunger), consumable eating, melee combat kills, loot roll counts + default-table fallback, day/night darkness range
Verified locally under -Werror with g++ 13: 36 checks, 0 failures

name: zomboid terminal front-end
observations: apps/zomboid-tui/main.cpp — the first PLAYABLE build of the native Zomboid port (CMake target zomboid_tui, output 'zomboid-tui'), POSIX-only (termios), added to root CMake under if(NOT WIN32)
Puts the terminal in raw mode (ICANON/ECHO off, VMIN/VTIME 0 non-blocking), uses the alt screen + hides cursor, restores on exit/atexit/SIGINT/SIGTERM

Real-time fixed-step loop (accumulator, ~30fps nanosleep pacing); maps keyboard into zb::Input — WASD movement (held-window ~160ms to smooth terminal key-repeat), SPACE attack (held), E/R/F and 1-8 and P/N as debounced edges (180ms). Aims at nearest zombie within 8 tiles else last heading. N starts a new game (also restarts after death), Q quits

Renders the SoftRenderer Framebuffer as truecolor half-block ANSI: each char cell is U+2580 with fg=top pixel, bg=bottom pixel (two pixels per row), with fg/bg escape-code change minimization; plus a 3-line text HUD (HP/FED/HYD/ENE/MOOD, DAY/clock/KILLS/Z/WEAPON, controls). Renders with hud=false/postFx=false at tilePx=5, sized to the live terminal (ioctl TIOCGWINSZ)

--once [--frames N] is a headless smoke path (no termios/TTY): runs autopilot then prints one ANSI frame + status and exits 0; auto-selected when stdin isn't a TTY. Wired as ctest zomboid_tui_smoke (NOT WIN32). Verified locally: clean under g++ and clang with -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror; --once emits a valid ~37KB truecolor frame and the text HUD
